content:
A sending church can gather its own people, pray, and send you before Launch Sunday. Plan that as its own service with that church. Do not tuck it into a rehearsal or a short slot on launch day.

You do not write the prayers or pick the practices. The sending church does, inside its own tradition. You ask early, hold the date, and make room for that congregation. Everyfield does not judge calling, character, or fitness, and this service is not a requirement for the next phase.

---

## Give the sending congregation its own service

A congregation cannot really take part if commissioning is only a private prayer, or a few minutes inside another gathering. Give the people who have supported you a service on their calendar, with their leaders in front.

Two plans you already have stay in place. The night before Launch Sunday, the Launch Team still gathers for worship, communion, and a commissioning prayer with laying on of hands, then goes home to rest. [Launch Team Spiritual Preparation](/wiki/pre-launch/launch-team-spiritual-preparation) describes that night. Keep it encouraging, not logistical.

Launch Sunday can still include a partner greeting or a short blessing. [Partner Organization Coordination](/wiki/launch-sunday/partner-organization-coordination) already lists formal commissioning as one possible role that day. The earlier service does not cancel that greeting.

Holding this service does not prove the plant is ready. Missing it does not, by itself, hold a phase back. You plan it because a church is sending people, not because software is scoring you.

<Callout type="insight">
A sending service marks a relationship between churches. It does not measure church health, and it does not show that shepherding, membership, or pastoral care are already in place. Those take longer than one afternoon.
</Callout>

---

## Ask the sending church to lead

If a church has taken responsibility for sending you, ask its leaders for a public time of affirmation, prayer, and sending before Launch Sunday. They choose who speaks, what is prayed, and which practices fit their church.

They may lay hands on the people being sent, read a charge, share communion, or pray and ask the congregation to stand with you. Accept the answer. Do not bring another church's order of service, and do not ask them to copy a script from somewhere else.

Say who you hope will be sent: the Senior Pastor, the household, the Launch Team, or some of these. They may narrow the list. Receive that decision. Do not turn it into a verdict on anyone's worth.

In Acts 13, while the church at Antioch was ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said to set apart Barnabas and Saul for the work to which the Spirit had called them. The church then fasted, prayed, laid hands on them, and sent them away. Acts later says they had been committed to the grace of God for that work, from Antioch. That is a picture, not a script. Your host decides what to carry into its own gathering.

---

## If no church has sent you

Some plants have no congregation that calls itself the sending church. A network, a few friends, or a Core Group may be the real story. Do not invent a sending church so the afternoon looks settled.

Ask one partner congregation to host, and let its leaders choose the form. If it agrees, say in the service that this church is hosting and praying with you. Call it a sending church only if its leaders use that name for themselves.

If no church will host, the Senior Pastor and the other responsible local leaders can still gather the people who have walked with the plant. Pray, speak plainly about the work, and say who is actually in the room. A circle of friends is not a sending church. A staff briefing in a side room is not this service either.

<Callout type="warning">
Do not ask Everyfield, a form, or a set of notes to decide who should be sent. Calling, character, and fitness belong in a human conversation among church leaders. Everyfield will not write the prayers, judge spiritual health, or certify anyone you present.
</Callout>

---

## Settle the plans you own

You own the asking. The host owns the service.

- [ ] Name the host church, or the local leaders if no church will host.
- [ ] Ask for a date before Launch Sunday, on the host's calendar.
- [ ] Say who you hope they will send, and accept their revision.
- [ ] Ask what they need from you, such as names or a short account of the work.
- [ ] Agree whether anyone from the plant will speak, and for how long.
- [ ] Confirm the congregation, or the real supporting circle, is invited.
- [ ] Leave the night-before prayer and the Launch Sunday greeting on their own plans.
- [ ] Thank the host in writing afterward.

Bring the questions below. Do not answer them for the host.

| Question | Leave this with the host |
|---|---|
| Who leads and who prays | Their own leaders |
| Which practices they will use | Laying on of hands, a charge, communion, or prayer |
| Who should be in the room | Their congregation, not only staff |
| What they will not do | A blessing without the word commission |

---

## Set the date away from launch weekend

Ask for a date that misses the night before Launch Sunday and Launch Sunday itself. That night needs to stay worship and rest. Launch Sunday already has a place for partners. A third event in the same weekend will shrink all three.

[Pre-Launch Services](/wiki/pre-launch/pre-launch-services) are the wrong home for this too. Those evenings are Launch Team rehearsals. A sending congregation is not there to practice your rundown.

Prefer a Sunday or midweek date in the weeks before launch. If the only open date is in the final week, take it, and still protect the night before. Write the date on both calendars when you agree. If the host wants the Launch Team present, tell them early enough to travel. They come to be seen and sent, not to run the afternoon.

---

## Help their congregation take part

Ask how the host usually invites its own congregation, and use those channels. Offer a few sentences they can edit: who is going, where the new work is, and that the hour is for prayer and sending.

Do not turn their service into a launch advertisement. The week before Launch Sunday you still send partner churches the date, the place, and a prayer request. Keep that announcement with partner coordination.

If the host wants a testimony, keep it short and let their leader introduce it. If they want none, give none.

<Callout type="important">
Do not assume this service makes anyone a minister for federal tax purposes. IRS Publication 517 describes ministers as individuals who are duly ordained, commissioned, or licensed by a religious body constituting a church or church denomination. Whether this afternoon does that depends on the host church's own practice, not on a planting checklist. If someone will be paid as a minister, have the church and a CPA review the current publication before you rely on this service. Checked October 26, 2026. Confirm the current text with the IRS.
</Callout>

---

## Leave status language with the church

Use the host's words. If they commission, use that word in their service, and be careful with it afterward. If they bless and send without it, do not upgrade the afternoon when you retell it.

Do not call the service an ordination, a background check, or a finding that someone is fit. Do not tell the new congregation that this hour means a healthy church already exists. You may be moving toward launch and still have years of care ahead. A note of who prayed, and what they asked, is enough for memory. It is not a score.

---

## After you are sent

Thank the host within a few days. If they offered to keep praying, tell them how. Do not hand them work they did not offer.

Tell the Launch Team what was prayed and what the host asked of them. Then go back to the final weeks: finish the rehearsals, keep the prayer rhythm you already planned, and confirm the partner greeting for Launch Sunday.

A church that sent you can still pray, visit, and tell the truth. Let them. They do not owe you a second ceremony on launch morning unless you planned that greeting together.

---

<Callout type="scripture">
*"Then, when they had fasted and prayed and laid their hands on them, they sent them away."* — Acts 13:3 (LSB)
</Callout>

rulings: Bryan ruled R7 = Option A: "Separate sending service" (2026-10-26 1:31 PM ET).
Wording call: title is Planning a Sending Service so the ruled form is visible in the title. Slug stays pre-launch/planning-a-commissioning-service, the slug suggested in the brief.
Wording call: sort_order 9, the next unused integer after the pre-launch articles at 1-8 in seed.json, and before the later promotion article at 20.

Wording call: the separate service does not replace the night-before commissioning prayer in pre-launch/launch-team-spiritual-preparation or a Launch Sunday partner greeting in launch-sunday/partner-organization-coordination. Those published practices stay.

Wording call: if no sending church exists, ask one partner congregation to host and choose the form. If none will, the Senior Pastor and responsible local leaders hold a public prayer and sending with the people who have actually walked with the plant, and they name that relationship honestly. Do not invent a sending church.

Wording call: do not prescribe laying on of hands, a charge, or communion for the sending service. The host church chooses. The night-before article already includes laying on of hands for the Launch Team prayer.

Constraint carried into the draft: this service is not an added phase criterion (REQ-PHASE-008) and does not establish church health or ecclesial readiness (Bryan C20). Everyfield and Evry do not judge calling, character, fitness, or spiritual health, and do not compose the prayers (REQ-EVR-001).
Wording call: a short IRS Publication 517 warning is included so the word commissioned is not read as a tax status. The article is not tax advice.
Background only, not a source: Hernandez, Churches Plant Churches (NAMB, 2026) ch. 4. Text was not copied and the book is not listed in draft.sources.
